newsitem.title: ITALY: Libya opposes "punitive" environmental oil taxes.
newsitem.headline: Libya opposes "punitive" environmental oil taxes.

text.p: Libya on Wednesday urged oil producers to present a united opposition to what it called punitive environment-related legislation and tax policies being adopted in some industrial countries.
Libya's OPEC governor Ali Fituri was addressing the Offshore Mediterranean Conference, reading a speech by Libyan energy minister Abdullah Salem al-Badri who was unable to attend.

"Oil is already heavily taxed and we in OPEC believe that the proposed tax is but another form of excise tax intended to raise government receipts from oil which, in many countries including Italy, are already more than three times the petroleum export revenues of the oil producing developing countries," Fituri said.
"Alternatively, we find the other sources of energy are either not taxed as heavily or, in the case of coal, are subsidised," he added.
"We need to present a united opposition to the punitive legislation and tax policies being adopted in a number of industrialised countries."

On oil prices, the speech said, "We in OPEC continue to work towards stable and reasonable prices. Price stability is a common interest for both the producing countries and the consumers," it concluded.

Libya is the largest offshore oil producer in the Mediterranean with current output of 53,000 barrels per day. This is set to increase in the long term because of Libya's proven oil reserves such as the Bouri field, Fituri said.
